headline: No meaningful interaction risk: both agents are docs-only, non-runnable, and expose no shared channels or write/network capabilities.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Neither agent has clipboard, stdin/stdout, filesystem, MCP, or browser surfaces, so there is no plausible channel for one agent’s output to be injected into the other by default. LlamaFactory is non-runnable and python-cheatsheet is documentation-only, so interaction is blocked.
conditions: IF either agent is later connected through a shared clipboard, file bridge, or MCP server, reassess injection risk.
mitigations: Keep the pair disconnected from shared copy/paste workflows.
Do not add a shared filesystem mount.
Do not enable MCP or browser bridging.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a bridge is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both profiles show no filesystem read/write, no network egress, no APIs, and no secrets or data classes touched. With no shared workspace or outbound channel, there is no plausible data leakage path between LlamaFactory and python-cheatsheet.
conditions: IF either agent is granted filesystem access or outbound network access, re-evaluate leakage risk.
mitigations: Keep both agents offline.
Avoid placing sensitive files in any shared directory.
Do not grant API credentials to either agent.
requires-engineering: add DLP controls before enabling any shared storage.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: There is no overlapping write authority: both agents have write_filesystem false, modify_git_state false, and no network or subprocess capabilities. python-cheatsheet also cannot support multiple instances, but that is irrelevant because neither agent can mutate shared state.
conditions: IF either agent gains write access to the same directory or git repo, reassess conflict risk.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only.
Avoid shared mutable repositories.
Do not enable concurrent write workflows.
requires-engineering: introduce locking if write access is added.

D_cascading_error.rationale: The pair cannot form a harmful action chain because neither agent can execute tools, access files, or call APIs, and both are documentation-only/non-runnable. There is no evidence that python-cheatsheet would treat LlamaFactory output as authoritative in an operational sense.
conditions: IF a downstream orchestrator starts treating one agent’s text as executable instructions, reassess cascading-error risk.
mitigations: Require human review of any generated text.
Do not auto-execute outputs.
Keep both agents in documentation-only mode.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before any downstream action.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data classes, residency constraints, or retention policies are exposed in either profile, and both agents are open-source docs-only artifacts. With no PHI, EU PII, or secrets handled, there is no compliance mismatch to assess.
conditions: IF either agent is later assigned regulated data classes such as PHI or EU PII, reassess compliance risk.
mitigations: Do not route regulated data to either agent.
Document data-class handling before deployment.
Keep retention policies unchanged for now.
requires-engineering: perform a formal compliance review if regulated data is introduced.
